The test image shows soybean leaves with:
- Small, scattered reddish-brown to dark brown spots across all leaflets
- A grayish/dusty coating visible on portions of the leaf surface (particularly the lower leaflet)
- Angular to circular small lesions
- Leaf is otherwise green without major yellowing

Top candidates: **Downy_mildew** (grayish coating on leaf surface) or **Septoria_brown_spot** (small angular reddish-brown spots). Let me check the Downy mildew reference since the grayish coating is the most distinctive feature.

The Downy mildew reference shows pale yellow-green spots on upper surface — very different from the test image.

**Revised analysis**: The test image features small, angular, dark reddish-brown spots scattered across all leaflets on an otherwise green leaf — this matches **Septoria_brown_spot** precisely: "Angular, red to brown spots varying from tiny specks to quarter-inch diameter appear on upper and lower leaf surfaces." The grayish tinge on the lower leaflet is consistent with early deposition or shadowing, not mold growth. No pale yellow halos (bacterial blight), no reddish-purple ring (frogeye), no powdery coating (powdery mildew).
